concepts.definition: The three message types the radio can carry.
concepts.example: A number is used for a command, text for a greeting, and a name = value pair for a reading such as "sicak = 28".
concepts.pitfall: Trying to send everything as a number; the receiving side cannot tell what was measured.

concepts.definition: A message made of a label (name) and a number (value).
concepts.example: radio send [sicak] = [28]; the receiving side reads received name and received value.
concepts.pitfall: Writing the name differently on the two sides; "sicak" and `sıcak` do not match.

concepts.definition: A text can be at most 32 characters and a name at most 12 characters; anything longer is cut off.
concepts.example: Of a 40-letter text, only the first 32 letters arrive on the receiving card.
concepts.pitfall: Choosing a long name; the cut-off name does not match the full name on the receiving side.

concepts.definition: A simple way to tell whether the message that arrived is a name = value message. In number and text messages the name is empty.
concepts.example: if received name = sicak then show the value, else show the text.
concepts.pitfall: Reading the same block for every message; you need to choose the block that fits the message type.

concepts.definition: A block that gives how strongly the message arrived. In the virtual radio it is always 200.
concepts.example: On a real radio, the value drops as the cards move further apart.
concepts.pitfall: Expecting the signal strength to change in the virtual portal; there is no distance.

quiz.prompt: A card wants to send the temperature, the light and the sound level to the other card at the same time. Which is the best method?
options: Sending the three numbers one after another as plain numbers
Writing them all in one text
Using a different name for each reading and sending name = value messages
quiz.explanation: To tell the three readings apart, each one is given its own name (sicak, isik, ses) and name = value messages are used; the receiving side looks at the name and puts the value in the right place. If you send three plain numbers, it gets mixed up which one measures what.

quiz.prompt: A card sends a 40-character text by radio. How many characters of the text arrive on the receiving card?
quiz.explanation: A text can be at most 32 characters; anything longer is cut off while being sent, without an error. 40 − 32 = 8 characters are lost.

quiz.prompt:
The receiving card's program is below. The sending card sends radio send [isik] = [90]. What happens on the receiving card?

```
on radio received:
    if received name = sicak then
        show number received value
    else
        show text received text
```
options: The then branch runs and 90 appears
The else branch runs, because the name is isik and not sicak
quiz.explanation: The name of the message that arrived is isik, but the name being checked is sicak; they are not equal, so the else branch runs. Even if the message is a name = value message, the then branch is skipped if the name does not match. No error appears, and the answer "nothing happens" is wrong too: the else branch shows something.

quiz.prompt:
The sender sends the temperature reading, but the receiving card always shows text on the screen (the then branch never runs). Find the mistake.

```
sender:    radio send [sıcak] = [temperature]
receiver:  if received name = sicak then ...
```
options: The name is written differently on the two sides: `sıcak` and `sicak` are not the same
The sending block was taken from the wrong category
The value must be a number, and temperature is not a number
quiz.explanation: The sender writes `sıcak` (with the letter `ı`), and the receiver writes `sicak` (with the letter `i`). Names must be exactly the same, letter for letter; a difference of one letter breaks the equality. The groups and the value block are not the cause of the problem.

quiz.prompt: The sender sends radio send [sicaklik_olcum] = [25]. The receiving side compares "received name = sicaklik_olcum". What is the result?
options: Equal, because the name is the same
Not equal, because the name is cut off to 12 characters
quiz.explanation: sicaklik_olcum is 14 characters, but the name limit is 12. While being sent, it is cut off to "sicaklik_olc". Because the cut-off name does not match the full name on the receiving side, the comparison comes out false, and no error message is given.
